editorial.headline: Performance Arts: Nationally Open, but Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Performance arts are nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent moratorium prevents PMA registration for this activity.
editorial.body:
**A foreign investor cannot register this performance-arts activity as PMA in Bali today.** That is the practical conclusion, even though the activity is nationally open and permits up to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, the OSS risk assessment at the Besar scale is Low or Medium-Low across every scope in this activity. That brings it within the island-wide, permanent Bali moratorium barring PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk activities, recorded here as taking effect on May thirteen, twenty twenty-six.

The activity itself is broad, but coherent: it is the presentation of artistic and stage entertainment by individuals or groups. It encompasses drama and theatre, music performances and concerts, opera, pantomime, dance, and regional art performances including wayang orang and lenong. It also covers groups such as circuses, orchestras and bands; individual performers including actors, stand-up comedians, dancers, singers, musicians, backing singers and conductors; and wayang performances led by a dalang. Monologues, dramatic readings and poetry set to music sit within the same field.

The scope also recognises the contemporary working lives of performance practitioners. Photo models, influencers, content creators and YouTubers appearing in vlogs or other content are included, as are independent musicians and actors visible across video and audiovisual content. A group may operate an arts facility for its own artistic group. Registration is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so the national classification accommodates both individual creative practice and larger organised performance operations.

That national openness should not be mistaken for Bali availability. A 100% foreign-ownership ceiling nationally does not displace the Bali restriction: the decisive local fact is the Low or Medium-Low OSS risk profile at the Besar scale, and the moratorium applies island-wide and permanently. For a foreign-owned registration in Bali, the current answer is therefore not conditional or procedural; this activity is blocked.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not displace Bali’s permanent bar on PMA registration for this activity.
